target.title: security(audit): warn on plugin load paths and SecretRef env fallback
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes two operator visibility gaps in OpenClaw security posture checks:

1. **`plugins.load.paths` trust-boundary risk** — Operators can point `plugins.load.paths` at arbitrary local directories, but `openclaw security audit` did not evaluate those configured paths for filesystem risk (world-writable paths, missing entries, bundled aliases, synced folders) before runtime plugin load.
2. **SecretRef env fallback visibility** — Runtime secret resolution can fall back to environment variables in some configurations; operators lacked a dedicated audit finding when that fallback was active.

**Concrete example:** An operator adds a world-writable `/tmp/demo-plugin` to `plugins.load.paths` and configures gateway auth via SecretRef that silently resolves from `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN`. Before this PR, `openclaw security audit` did not surface either risk explicitly.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds `collectPluginLoadPathAuditFindings` and wires SecretRef env-fallback diagnostics into `openclaw security audit` / doctor health contributions so misconfiguration surfaces as explicit findings instead of silent trust expansion.

Two correctness issues from ClawSweeper review were also fixed in this revision:
- **Restored `doctor:default-account-routing` contribution** — the initial squash accidentally dropped the existing opt-in doctor lint contribution for multi-account default routing; it is now preserved alongside the new `core/doctor/secretref-env-fallback` check added to `doctor:gateway-auth`.
- **Env propagation fix** — `isActiveGatewayTokenSurface` in `secretref-env-fallback-diagnostics.ts` now accepts and forwards the caller-provided `env` to `resolveGatewayAuth`, preventing ambient `process.env` from being used for the auth-mode guard when an explicit env is injected by audit or doctor.

## User Impact

**Before:** Risky plugin load paths and active SecretRef env fallbacks could go unnoticed.

**After:** `openclaw security audit` emits `plugins.load_paths.*` and `GATEWAY_AUTH_TOKEN_SECRETREF_ENV_FALLBACK` findings operators can act on. No runtime behavior change unless operators remediate.

## Evidence

- `src/security/audit-plugin-load-paths.ts:55` — `collectPluginLoadPathFindings`
- `src/security/audit-secretref-env-fallback.ts` — maps shared diagnostics to audit findings
- `src/secrets/secretref-env-fallback-diagnostics.ts` — shared diagnostic collector (env propagation fix at `isActiveGatewayTokenSurface`)
- `src/flows/doctor-health-contributions.ts` — `doctor:default-account-routing` contribution restored
- Diff: +794 / −145 across audit, doctor, secrets, and docs (squashed single commit `0769826`)

### Real behavior proof (commit `0769826`, macOS, paths redacted)

#### 1) New doctor checks registered and running

```text
$ openclaw doctor --lint --all --only core/doctor/default-account-routing --json
{"ok":true,"checksRun":1,"checksSkipped":51,"findings":[]}

$ openclaw doctor --lint --all --only core/doctor/secretref-env-fallback --json
{"ok":true,"checksRun":1,"checksSkipped":51,"findings":[]}
```

Both `core/doctor/default-account-routing` (restored) and `core/doctor/secretref-env-fallback` (new) are registered and execute without error. No findings emitted on this operator's config (no env-fallback SecretRef token configured, no multi-account routing gap).

#### 2) `openclaw security audit --deep` (real CLI, personal config, private paths redacted)

```text
$ openclaw security audit --deep

OpenClaw security audit
Summary: 3 critical · 3 warn · 1 info
Run deeper: openclaw security audit --deep

CRITICAL
security.exposure.open_groups_with_elevated  Open group/DM policy with elevated tools enabled
  Found inbound policy="open" at: channels.telegram.groupPolicy
  With tools.elevated enabled, a prompt injection in those conversations can become a high-impact incident.

security.exposure.open_groups_with_runtime_or_fs  Open group/DM policy with runtime/filesystem tools exposed
  Found inbound policy="open" at: channels.telegram.groupPolicy
  Risky tool exposure contexts:
  - agents.defaults (sandbox=off; runtime=[exec, process]; fs=[read, write, edit, apply_patch]; fs.workspaceOnly=false)

WARN
gateway.trusted_proxies_missing  Reverse proxy headers are not trusted
security.trust_model.multi_user_heuristic  Potential multi-user setup detected (personal-assistant model warning)

INFO
summary.attack_surface  Attack surface summary
  groups: open=1, allowlist=0 · tools.elevated: enabled · browser control: enabled
```

Audit runs cleanly with the new collectors wired in. No `plugins.load_paths.*` findings on this config (no custom `plugins.load.paths` entries). No `GATEWAY_AUTH_TOKEN_SECRETREF_ENV_FALLBACK` finding (gateway token not via SecretRef env fallback on this install).

#### 3) Regression tests (Vitest, real run on commit `0769826`)

```text
$ pnpm test src/security/audit-plugin-load-paths.test.ts \
            src/security/audit-secretref-env-fallback.test.ts

 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  4 passed (4)
   Duration  3.91s

$ pnpm test src/secrets/secretref-env-fallback-diagnostics.test.ts

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  4 passed (4)
   Duration  348ms

$ pnpm test src/flows/doctor-health-contributions.test.ts

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  87 passed (87)
   Duration  1.97s
```

All 95 tests pass across the four test files. `doctor-health-contributions.test.ts` includes coverage for `doctor:default-account-routing` (restored contribution) and `core/doctor/secretref-env-fallback` (new gateway-auth health check).

Regression flows covered by tests:

| Collector | Scenario | Expected finding |
|-----------|----------|------------------|
| `collectPluginLoadPathFindings` | world-writable temp dir in `plugins.load.paths` | `plugins.load_paths.world_writable` |
| `collectPluginLoadPathFindings` | nonexistent path in `plugins.load.paths` | `plugins.load_paths.missing` (warn) |
| `collectSecretRefEnvFallbackDiagnostics` | gateway token resolves from `env` via SecretRef | `GATEWAY_AUTH_TOKEN_SECRETREF_ENV_FALLBACK` at `gateway.auth.token` |
| `isActiveGatewayTokenSurface` with injected env | caller-provided env forwarded to `resolveGatewayAuth` | correct auth-mode guard without ambient `process.env` leak |
| `doctor:default-account-routing` | multi-account channel config, no explicit default | `core/doctor/default-account-routing` warning (opt-in, `defaultEnabled: false`) |
